roleTitle: Mobile Application Engineer, Enterprise Knowledge Base
jobDescription: The enterprise knowledge base product gives field staff offline access to procedures, parts data and safety notices on iOS and Android. The Mobile Application Engineer develops and maintains the offline sync and search features, works with the content team on release contents, and is expected to improve measurable app quality indicators such as crash-free sessions and sync failure rates against the product's published baselines.
requirements: Develops and maintains the offline sync and search features of the knowledge base app on iOS and Android.
Improves app quality indicators such as crash-free sessions or sync failure rate, reported against a documented baseline.
Coordinates release contents with the content team and records own responsibility boundaries for each release.
Investigates crash and sync reports from field staff and documents root causes.
Documents known limitations and hand-over conditions for each app release.

evidence.text: Developed the delta-sync module for the knowledge base app (Kotlin and Swift), replacing the full-catalogue download with change-set downloads and a resumable transfer when field devices lose connectivity.

Reduced the sync failure rate from 6.8 percent to 2.1 percent of sync attempts between the March and June releases, measured by the app analytics dashboard against the product's published baseline of 6.8 percent for the January to February period.
Coordinated release contents with the content team for four releases; my part covered the sync and search changes, while the release manager decided the release date and scope.
Triaged crash and sync reports from field staff through the support queue, documenting root causes in the engineering wiki and linking each to the fixing change.
Responsibilities included offline sync development, quality-indicator reporting, release coordination and support triage for the knowledge base app over about two years.

Work sample: the sync-failure-rate report exported from the app analytics dashboard (weekly rate, attempts, baseline line, release markers for March and June) and the delta-sync design note, with the dashboard export identifiers as a verification trail.

Reference call with former engineering manager: confirmed employment dates (two years and one month), the delta-sync work and that the sync-failure figures came from the team's shared analytics dashboard.
Recruiter logistics note: notice period is one month; the candidate can attend an on-site technical session in the next two weeks.

gold.expectedGap: Hand-over conditions for each release are only partly documented; the materials cover release coordination but not the hand-over notes.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the quantified result as stated, with its baseline, window and measurement source; do not extend it to other quality indicators or to releases outside March to June.
